SMTO-SKL-0024 — Google is limiting how fast SMTO can use your calendar

GUID: 7600f771-68cb-53de-bc69-de07905edf67
Slug: google-calendar-provider-rate-limited
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google is temporarily refusing calendar requests because too many were sent in a short time, or a usage limit was reached. Google turned this one away, so it didn't happen.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few minutes before asking SMTO for more calendar work. Google's limit resets after a short time.
  2. Break large requests into smaller ones, such as fewer days to search or fewer events to change at once. Smaller requests send fewer calls to Google and are less likely to hit the limit.
  3. If you asked for a change, check Google Calendar to confirm it isn't there yet, then ask SMTO to make it again. Google refused this change, but checking first avoids making it twice if another request already did.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the calendar task without this message.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps happening, the Google app used by SMTO may need a higher limit. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Calendar returned 429 or a rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded or quotaExceeded reason; reads were retried up to twice only when the Retry-After delay allowed, and writes are never retried.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 429 or a rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded or quotaExceeded reason. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 429 or a rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded or quotaExceeded reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded quota reason and Retry-After without confusing it with missing consent.

How to fix it

  • Wait for the provider quota window or Retry-After interval before another operation; reads retry automatically only for short delays, and writes are never replayed. Reduce request volume (smaller windows, fewer pages), and for persistent limits check the Google Cloud project's Calendar API quota.
  • Wait for the provider quota or Retry-After interval before requesting another operation. Only bounded reads retry automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Wait for the provider quota or Retry-After interval before requesting another operation. Only bounded reads retry automatically.

How to verify the fix

  • A later authorized operation respects the provider interval and bounded read retry policy.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
